questions.stem:
The incorrect postulates of the Dalton's atomic theory are :
(A) Atoms of different elements differ in mass.
(B) Matter consists of divisible atoms.
(C) Compounds are formed when atoms of different element combine in a fixed ratio.

questions.stem: Identify compound (Z) in the following reaction sequence.

Given below are two statements : One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R)
Assertion (A): Enthalpy of neutralisation of strong monobasic acid with strong monoacidic base is always $-57\ \mathrm{kJ\,mol^{-1}}$
Reason (R): Enthalpy of neutralisation is the amount of heat liberated when one mole of $\mathrm{H^{+}}$ ions furnished by acid combine with one mole of $\mathrm{{}^{-}OH}$ ions furnished by base to form one mole of water.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.solution: Enthalpy of neutralization of SA & SB is always $-57\ \mathrm{kJ/mol}$ because strong monoacid gives one mole of $\mathrm{H^{+}}$ and strong mono base gives one mole of $\mathrm{OH^{-}}$ which form one mole of water.

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)

questions.stem:
The statement(s) that are correct about the species $\mathrm{O^{2-}}$, $\mathrm{F^{-}}$, $\mathrm{Na^{+}}$ and $\mathrm{Mg^{2+}}$.
(A) All are isoelectronic
(B) All have the same nuclear charge
(C) $\mathrm{O^{2-}}$ has the largest ionic radii
(D) $\mathrm{Mg^{2+}}$ has the smallest ionic radii
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :

For the compounds:
(A) $\mathrm{H_3C-CH_2-O-CH_2-CH_2-CH_3}$
(B) $\mathrm{H_3C-CH_2-CH_2-CH_2-CH_3}$
(C) $\mathrm{CH_3-CH_2-C(=O)-CH_2-CH_3}$
(D) $\mathrm{H_3C-CH(OH)-CH_2-CH_2-CH_3}$
The increasing order of boiling point is :
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.solution:
Compounds having same number of carbon atoms follow the boiling point order as:
$(\text{Boiling point})_{\text{Hydrogen bonding}} > (\text{Boiling point})_{\text{high polarity}} > (\text{Boiling point})_{\text{low polarity}} > (\text{Boiling point})_{\text{non polar}}$

questions.stem:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I: In group 13, the stability of $+1$ oxidation state increases down the group.
Statement II: The atomic size of gallium is greater than that of aluminium.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Statement I : Number of d & f electrons, increases down the group and due to poor shielding of d & f $e^{-}$, stability of lower oxidation states increases down the group
Statement II : The atomic size of aluminium is greater than that of gallium

options.text: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect

questions.stem:
Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): Cis form of alkene is found to be more polar than the trans form
Reason (R): Dipole moment of trans isomer of 2-butene is zero.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
Dipole moment is a vector quantity and for compound net dipole moment is the vector sum of all dipoles hence dipole moment of cis form is greater than trans form.
Cis ($\mu > 0$) $>$ trans ($\mu = 0$)

options.text: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)

questions.stem:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I: Nitration of benzene involves the following step –
Statement II: Use of Lewis base promotes the electrophilic substitution of benzene.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
questions.solution:
In nitration of benzene concentrated $\mathrm{H_2SO_4}$ and $\mathrm{HNO_3}$ is used as reagent which generates electrophile $\mathrm{N\overset{\oplus}{O}_2}$ in following steps:
$\mathrm{H_2SO_4 + HNO_3 \rightleftharpoons HSO_4^{\ominus} + H-\overset{H}{\underset{\oplus}{O}}-NO_2 \rightleftharpoons HSO_4^{\ominus} + H_2O + NO_2^{\oplus}}$
Lewis acids can promote the formation of electrophiles not Lewis base

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct

questions.stem: Molar ionic conductivities of divalent cation and anion are $57\ \mathrm{S\ cm^{2}\ mol^{-1}}$ and $73\ \mathrm{S\ cm^{2}\ mol^{-1}}$ respectively. The molar conductivity of solution of an electrolyte with the above cation and anion will be :

The number of neutrons present in the more abundant isotope of boron is 'x'. Amorphous boron upon heating with air forms a product, in which the oxidation state of boron is 'y'. The value of $x + y$ is …
questions.solution:
More abundant isotope = $\mathrm{B^{11}}$
[Number of neutrons = 6]
$x = 6$
$\mathrm{B + O_2 \rightarrow B_2O_3}$
Oxidation state of B in $\mathrm{B_2O_3}$ = +3
So, $y = 3$
Hence $x + y = 9$

questions.stem: The value of Rydberg constant ($R_H$) is $2.18\times10^{-18}$ J. The velocity of electron having mass $9.1\times10^{-31}$ kg in Bohr's first orbit of hydrogen atom = ……… $\times 10^{5}\ \mathrm{ms^{-1}}$ (nearest integer)
questions.solution:
$V = 2.18 \times 10^{6} \times \frac{Z}{n}$
$= 21.8 \times 10^{5} \times \frac{1}{1} \approx 22 \times 10^{5}$ (nearest)

[Given atomic number of Cu = 29, Ni = 28, Mn = 25, Fe = 26]
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{Fe^{3+}}$ will give green coloured bead when heated at point B.
Number of unpaired $e^{-}$ in $\mathrm{Fe^{3+}} = 5$
$\mu = 5.92$
Nearest integer = 6

questions.stem: The heat of combustion of solid benzoic acid at constant volume is $-321.30$ kJ at $27^\circ$C. The heat of combustion at constant pressure is $(-321.30 - xR)$ kJ, the value of x is …………….
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{C_6H_5COOH(s) + \frac{15}{2}O_2(g) \rightarrow 7CO_2(g) + 3H_2O(\ell)}$
$\Delta H = \Delta U + \Delta n_g RT$
$= -321.30 - \frac{1}{2}\frac{R}{100} \times 300$
$= (-321.30 - 150R)$ kJ

questions.stem:
The spin only magnetic moment value of the ion among $\mathrm{Ti^{2+}}$, $\mathrm{V^{2+}}$, $\mathrm{Co^{3+}}$ and $\mathrm{Cr^{2+}}$, that acts as strong oxidising agent in aqueous solution is ……….. BM (Near integer).
(Given atomic numbers : Ti : 22, V : 23, Cr : 24, Co : 27)
questions.solution:
Strong oxidising agent = $\mathrm{Co^{+3}}$
No. of unpaired $e^{-}$ in $\mathrm{Co^{+3}[3d^{6}]} = 4$
Hence $\mu = \sqrt{n(n+2)} = \sqrt{24}$ BM
Nearest integer = 5

questions.stem:
During Kinetic study of reaction $\mathrm{2A + B \rightarrow C + D}$, the following results were obtained :
 | $A[M]$ | $B[M]$ | initial rate of formation of D
I | 0.1 | 0.1 | $6.0 \times 10^{-3}$
II | 0.3 | 0.2 | $7.2 \times 10^{-2}$
III | 0.3 | 0.4 | $2.88 \times 10^{-1}$
IV | 0.4 | 0.1 | $2.40 \times 10^{-2}$
Based on above data, overall order of the reaction is ……….

An artificial cell is made by encapsulating 0.2 M glucose solution within a semipermeable membrane. The osmotic pressure developed when the artificial cell is placed within a 0.05 M solution of NaCl at 300 K is _______ $\times 10^{-1}$ bar. (Nearest Integer)
[Given : $R = 0.083\ \mathrm{L\ bar\ mol^{-1}\ K^{-1}}$]
Assume complete dissociation of NaCl
questions.solution:
0.2 M Glucose (inside the cell) | 0.05 M NaCl Sol. (outside)
$\mathrm{NaCl \longrightarrow Na^{+} + Cl^{-}}$
$0.05\,\mathrm{M}$ | $0.05\,\mathrm{M}$ | $0.05\,\mathrm{M}$
Total $C_1 = 0.05 + 0.05 = 0.1$ M (NaCl)
$C_2 = 0.2$ M (glucose)
$\pi = (C_2 - C_1)RT$
$= (0.2 - 0.1) \times 0.083 \times 300$
$= 2.49$ bar
$= 24.9 \times 10^{-1}$ bar

questions.stem: 9.3 g of pure aniline is treated with bromine water at room temperature to give a white precipitate of the product 'P'. The mass of product 'P' obtained is 26.4 g. The percentage yield is ……… %.
questions.solution: 93 g of aniline produces 330 g of 2, 4, 6-tribromoaniline. Hence 9.3 g of aniline should produce 33g of 2, 4, 6-tribromoaniline. Hence percentage yield $\frac{26.4 \times 100}{33} = 80\%$
